text:
- [LFAC.2.5.1] **Engine-side (primary):** the engine
  de-duplicates no-op reassertions as the correctness
  contract. For `String`, `Bool`, `TYPE_NAME`, and default
  `Int` / `Float` slots the comparison is exact equality; for a `Float` that
  is IEEE 754 `==`, so a reassertion that turns `0.0` into `-0.0` is a no-op
  ([LFAC.1.7.1]).
  For `Json` slots the comparison is deep structural
  equality: two values are equal iff they are the same kind and

  - two objects have the same set of keys and, under each key, equal
    values; member order carries no meaning;
  - two arrays have the same length and equal elements, position by
    position;
  - two strings have the same bytes, two booleans the same value, and two
    nulls are equal;
  - two integers have the same value, and two floats compare by IEEE 754
    `==`, so `0.0` equals `-0.0`.

  An integer and a float are different kinds, so `1` and `1.0` are not
  equal: a leaf keeps the kind it was written with ([LEXP.7.12.1]).

  For a slot with a declared `tolerance` ([LGRA.5.9]; on a unit-typed slot,
  in its base unit, [LUNI.7.4]), values within
  the tolerance are treated as equal. **The bound is INCLUSIVE**:
  the values are equal iff they are exactly equal or `|delta| <= tolerance`,
  so a change of exactly `tolerance` IS suppressed. Two equal infinities are therefore equal under any tolerance,
  though their `delta` is NaN. This matters in ordinary use rather than at a float
  edge — `tolerance` is declared on `Int` slots too, where a delta
  landing exactly on the bound is commonplace.

  When a reassertion is suppressed, `dwell` does not reset, no series sample is
  generated, and derived `logical` facts do not flicker.

  The comparison is over the author's slots. `ts` is not compared
  ([LFAC.9.1]): a reassertion that differs from the live fact only in `ts` is
  a no-op, and the live fact keeps its `ts`.

alloy.name: lfac_2_5_1__ts_is_not_compared
alloy.note: Two reassertions of one value onto one fact decide alike whatever ts each supplies and at whatever sample: the no-op test is a function of the compared value. Bounded: six of each sig; fails if a no-op is made to require the supplied ts equal the live one.

alloy.name: lfac_9_2__noop_keeps_ts
alloy.note: A suppressed reassertion leaves the live fact's ts, whatever it supplied: a reassertion that differs only in ts changes nothing. Bounded: six of each sig.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__live_val
idris.note: Whether some live fact of the kind carries the value.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__live_val_append_mono
idris.note: Appending a fact keeps every live value live.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__live_val_append_self
idris.note: Appending a fact makes its value live.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__live_val_frame
idris.note: Liveness of a value of another kind is untouched by a change confined to one kind.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__same_val_refl
idris.note: Exact equality is reflexive.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__live_val_frame_pred
idris.note: Whether a value is live for a kind outside the change is unchanged.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__after
idris.note: A suppressed no-op reassertion does nothing to the stamps: '`dwell` does not reset'.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__suppressed_keeps_stamps
idris.note: '`dwell` does not reset' when a reassertion is suppressed: every stamp is as it was, for every lifecycle, working memory, value and sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__three_asserts
idris.note: The suppressed reassertion at 5, executed: the stamp is still 3.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__a_member_more_differs
idris.note: 'The same set of keys' and 'the same length', executed: an object with a member more differs in either direction, and so does an array of another length or with its elements in another order.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__an_integer_is_not_a_float
idris.note: An integer and a float are different kinds, executed: 1 is not 1.0 and 0 is not 0.0, at the root and under a key.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__json_eq
idris.note: The `Json` comparison, the clause's four bullets: two objects the same set of keys with equal values under each, member order carrying no meaning; two arrays the same length with equal elements position by position; two strings the same text (one token), two Bools the same value, two nulls equal; two integers the same value and two floats IEEE `==`, so 0.0 equals -0.0; an integer and a float never equal. The zeros are executed in Main.idr, the rest here.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__json_eq_list
idris.note: Two arrays' elements, position by position, over equal lengths.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__member_covers
idris.note: Whether some member of the first object has the second's key and a value equal to its value.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__member_in
idris.note: Whether a member of the first object has, in the second, a member with its key and an equal value.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__member_order_carries_no_meaning
idris.note: Two objects with the same members in different orders are equal, executed.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__members_covered
idris.note: Every member of the second object has, in the first, a member with its key and an equal value -- the first object's values on the left of every equality, as in `lfac_2_5_1__members_in`, so the recursion is structural.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__members_in
idris.note: Every member of the first object has, in the second, a member with its key and an equal value.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_fact
idris.note: A reassertion equal in every slot is suppressed (`Nothing`, nothing to propagate) for the two `logical` lifecycles and never for explicit. Equality is exact; the per-slot `tolerance` rules and the suppression counter are not modelled.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__same_val
idris.note: Exact equality of slot values.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__val
idris.note: A fact's slot values, the pair the comparison is over.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert
idris.note: The no-op reassertion: an identical value is suppressed.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_view
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion leaves the view as it was.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_frame
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion leaves every chain.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_shapes
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion changes nothing, shapes included.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_rows_emitted
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion changes nothing, the row property included.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_inputs_ttl
idris.note: An entity re-asserted with its live payload and a relation re-asserted: the clause's suppressed no-ops, among the inputs. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_ready_ttl
idris.note: The clause's suppression executed: the entity's unchanged reassertion and the relation's second assertion leave working memory, the alpha memories and A's activations as they were. Computed.

idris.name: iret_11_3__assert_unfired
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion changes nothing, so every activation stays unfired.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__entity_noop_fires_once
idris.note: The clause's de-duplication on an entity with one payload: one firing. Executed.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__relation_noop_fires_once
idris.note: The clause's de-duplication on a relation: one fact, one activation, one firing. Executed.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_ordered
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion leaves the order as it was.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_sound
idris.note: A suppressed reassertion asserts no fact: the set is kept, and refuses nothing new.
